title: Build a Product Catalog: Types, Categories and Search

steps.text: A product catalog lists products that visitors can browse by category and find with search. In this video, you build one in Orchard Core, with content types, a taxonomy, the Media Library, and Search.
Every product has the same structure: a name, a price, a picture, and a category. A content type defines that structure, and the Content Types feature lets you build one in the admin.
A taxonomy holds the categories, and the Taxonomies feature manages it. The Media feature stores the pictures in the Media Library, so every product can show one.
The Search feature adds a search page, which finds products in an index. You build the types, the categories, the pictures, the products, and then the search.
Let's start with the Product type. Under Design, Content Definition, Content Types, you see the types of the site. Click Create new type.
Enter Product as the Display Name. The Technical Name fills in by itself. Click Create.
A type is made of parts. The Title part gives every product a name, so check Title and click Add Selected Parts.
The Parts list shows Product, the part that holds the fields of this type. A field stores a value, such as a price. Click Add Field.
Enter Price as the Display Name, choose Numeric Field, and click Save & Configure.
Set Scale to 2, so a price has two digits after the decimal point, and check Required. Then click Save.
Add a second field. Name it Image, choose Media Field, and click Save. By default, a Media Field accepts several pictures.
The type lists its fields and its parts. Click Save to return to the list of content types.
Categories are content items too, so each one needs a content type. Click Create new type, and enter Product Category as the Display Name.
Click Create, check Title, and click Add Selected Parts. A category only needs a title, so click Save.
A taxonomy holds the categories, as terms. Open Content, Content Items, click New, and choose Taxonomy.
Enter Product Categories as the Title. For Term Content Type, choose Product Category, which is the type of each term. Click Publish.
Open the taxonomy again with Edit. The Add Product Category button appears once the taxonomy is saved.
Click Add Product Category, enter Backpacks as the Title, and click Publish. The term appears in the taxonomy.
Add Tents and Sleeping Bags the same way. A term also has an Add button, which creates a child term below it.
The terms are saved in a draft of the taxonomy. Click Publish to publish the taxonomy with its terms.
Next, connect the Product type to the taxonomy. Open Content Types, click Edit on Product, and click Add Field.
Enter Category as the Display Name, choose Taxonomy Field, and click Save & Configure.
Select Product Categories as the Taxonomy. Check Unique, so a product has only one category, and click Save.
The Product type has three fields: Price, Image, and Category. Each field is saved as soon as you add it.

Product pictures belong in the Media Library. Open Tools, Features, search for Media Slugify, and click Enable. It gives uploaded files and folders web-friendly names, and leaves existing ones unchanged.
Open Media, Library. The folder tree starts with the Files folder. Use its folder menu, and choose Create a subfolder.
Enter Product Photos as the folder name, and click Ok. Media Slugify turns the name into product-photos.
Select the folder, and click Upload files. Choose the pictures of the products. Media Slugify renames each file, so Trail Backpack becomes trail-backpack.
Open Content, Content Items, click New, and choose Product. The editor shows the Title, and a field for the price, the image, and the category.
Enter Trail Backpack as the Title, and 89 as the Price.
For Image, click Add media. The Media Library opens in a window. Select the picture in the product-photos folder, and click OK.
For Category, choose Backpacks, one of the terms you added to the taxonomy.
The Save Draft button keeps a product unpublished, and with the default index settings, search does not find a draft. Click Publish instead. A message confirms that the product has been published.
Add the other products the same way. The list of content items shows the whole catalog.

chapters.title: Add search
chapters.subtitle: An index, a setting and a permission

steps.text: An index lists the words of your content, and each word points to the content items that contain it. The search page looks the words up in the index.
Search needs three steps. Create an index, choose it as the default search index in the site settings, and allow visitors to query it.
When a visitor searches, the page checks the permission, looks the words up in the default index, and shows each matching content item.
Lucene builds the index, and Search adds the search page. Open Tools, Features, search for Lucene, and click Enable.
Then enable the feature named Search. Both features depend on the Indexing feature, which provides index management.
Open Search, Indexes, and click Add index. In the list of sources, click Add for Content in Lucene, which indexes content items.
Enter products as the Index Name. Under Content types, check Product, and click Save. By default, only published versions are indexed.
The index appears in the list, and Orchard Core builds it in the background. Products you publish later are added to it.
Next, tell the search page which index to use. Open Settings, Search, Site Search.
Choose products as the Default search index, and enter Search products as the Placeholder. Click Save.
Visitors who are not signed in need permission to search. Open Access Control, Roles, and click Edit on Anonymous.
Type products in Search permissions, and allow Query 'products' Index. Click Save.
Open the search page of the site, at the address /search. Type backpack, and click Search.
The result shows the product with its title, price, picture, and category. Click the title to open the product page.
The product page shows the price, the picture, and the category. A visitor reaches it from the search results.
A word that no product contains shows a message instead: There are no such results.
A content type defines the products, a taxonomy groups them, the Media Library stores their pictures, and Search finds them. You configure each part in the admin.
You built a product catalog with a content type, a taxonomy, the Media Library, and Search. Thanks for watching.
